origin.description: Profile empirical exponential family log likelihood for a mean.
origin.usage:
EEF.profile(y, tmin = min(y) + 0.1, tmax = max(y) - 0.1, n.t = 25,
           u = function(y, t) y - t)

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: A vector or matrix of data.

arguments.name: tmin
arguments.text: Smallest parameter on the grid. It must be larger than min(y).

arguments.name: tmax
arguments.text: Largest parameter on the grid. It must be smaller than max(y).

arguments.name: n.t
arguments.text: Number of steps from tmin to tmax. The loop runs from 0 through n.t, so the matrix has n.t + 1 rows.

arguments.name: u
arguments.text: Function of the data and the parameter. The default is y - t.

origin.details: The profile is for the practicals in chapter 10 of Davison and Hinkley (1997). The source fits glm(zero ~ psi - 1, poisson(log)). zero in the boot namespace is a function, so the installed call stops before fitting.
origin.value: A matrix with n.t + 1 rows. Column 1 is the parameter. Columns 2 and 3 are two centered versions of the exponential family log likelihood. Column 4 is the Lagrange multiplier.

translation.description: Profile empirical exponential family log likelihood for a mean.

arguments.name: tmin
arguments.text: Smallest parameter on the grid. None uses min(y) + 0.1.

arguments.name: tmax
arguments.text: Largest parameter on the grid. None uses max(y) - 0.1.

arguments.name: n_t
arguments.text: Number of steps from tmin to tmax. The result has n_t + 1 rows.

arguments.name: u
arguments.text: Function of the data and the parameter. None uses y - t.

translation.details: Each grid point is a Poisson log-link fit of a zero response on psi with no intercept, which is the model the formula names. The mean is floored at double epsilon and the fit starts at log(0.1). Columns 2 and 3 are centered by subtracting their maxima.
translation.value: An array with n_t + 1 rows and 4 columns. Column 1 is the parameter. Columns 2 and 3 are the two centered log likelihoods. Column 4 is the coefficient.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from boot.profile import eef_profile

y = np.array([76, 79, 81, 79, 77, 79, 79, 78, 79, 82, 76, 73, 64], dtype=float)
print(eef_profile(y, n_t=5))
